OUR PARTNERS

See your plan.
Live in the OR.

SyncAR® Spine brings the surgeon’s plan into surgery in a live, interactive, and precise way, delivering the look and feel of open surgery through real-time XR visualization.

What this enables:

  • Real-time, plan-driven clarity
  • Confidence and control for complex spine cases
  • XR that turns planning into action

Transforming 2D Imaging Into 3D Surgical Clarity

Surgical Theater’s eXperiential Reality® platform utilizes AI to transform traditional 2D scans into interactive 3D models that support clinical decisions from the clinic to the OR.

Gary K. Steinburg, MD, PHD, Stanford

PlanXR™

Explore anatomy with XR technology to locate potential risks. Our surgeons harness this cutting-edge technology to craft precise surgical plans, utilizing patient-specific XR reconstructions for optimal surgical performance.

BrainSTORM™

Streamlines epilepsy care continuum by creating a platform that visualizes all the epilepsy patient’s data in a comprehensive easy-to-understand XR model.

Experience

SyncAR® Cranial

Explore
"We can simulate or rehearse the entire surgical procedure beforehand, so that when we get to the surgery it’s not a surprise, it’s as if we already performed the surgery before."
Gary K. Steinberg, MD, PHDStanford Neuroscience Health Center, Palo Alto, CA
"There's a lot of really important vital structures, nerves, blood vessels, organs that with x-ray you don't see, with small dissections in surgery you don't see. When you overlay the entirety of the anatomy on the patient, you're able to see those so that really drives up the safety"
Maziyar Kalani, MDMayo Clinic Spine Center, Phoenix, AZ
"Integrating augmented reality into the operating room has the potential to improve surgical precision and patient outcomes at hospitals around the world."
Burak Ozgur, MDHoag Spine Center, Newport Beach, CA
"The success of the surgery is determined before the surgeon walks in, and that’s why this technology is really, really helpful. I think that walking into the surgery with optimism, with hope, fundamentally changes the trajectory of the patient’s health care journey."
Clark C. Chen, MD, PHD Masonic Cancer Center, Minneapolis, MN
"You're taking 2D images and converting them to multi-colored 3D renderings in VR…It's much easier for them to comprehend, for example, where a tumor is and what it does. It's also much easier for doctors to explain the intervention."
Walter C. JeanLehigh Valley Health Network, Allentown, PA
"In a case like this one, you need to go into surgery with a clear plan and a realistic assessment of potential pitfalls. It’s like a military operation—you really need to know what your contingencies are, so you don’t get in there and realize there are land mines you didn’t expect"
Anthony K. Frempong-Boadu, MDNYU Langone Health Comprehensive Neurofibromatosis Center, Manhattan, NY
"You can see your instruments in relation to the map of the brain and know exactly where you are. You can see around corners and see through tissue."
Joshua B. Bederson, MDThe Mount Sinai Hospital – Neurosurgery, Manhattan, NY
“I’m a believer. As we do more complex cases, I’m realizing the value of having the Surgical Theater’s 360° XR visualization platform. Patients appreciate it; it definitely wows them, but it is far more than that. Patients really understand better. They can see the relationship between the skull base tumor and surrounding important structures such as the optic nerve and carotid artery."
Mas Takashima, MDHouston Methodist – Dept. of Otolaryngology Head & Neck Surgery, Houston, TX
"This gives me what I like to call Superman vision which allows me to kind of see structures that I’m not able to see. To see through things, what’s around, what’s on the other side of a tumor."
Robert G. Louis, MDHoag Spine Center, Newport Beach, CA
